(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in nature of Mandamus commanding the respondent no. 2 to award appropriate compensation with interest of 18 percent as per Rule to petitioner from the period when the proposal was approved, by acquisition of his land Gata No. 523/0.126 (10 Biswa) for purposes of construction of Higher Primary School and after approval of proposal dated 17.01.2010 passed by Land Management Committee, Pure Boodhi Upadyay, District Amethi OR to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the respondent no.
2 to provide alternate land of same area & valuation and in same village to the petitioner in exchange of his land Gata No. 523/0.126(10 Biswa) used for construction of Higher Primary School in Vikas Khand Jaamo, Gram Panchayat Shahpur, Pure Boodhi Upadhyay, District Amethi.
(iii) to issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of Mandamus commanding the respondent to provide compensation for remaining land of 6 biswa used by respondents as per original agreement dated 17.01.2010 till passing of order dated 18.012.2022 of acquiring only 4 biswa of his land Gata No. 523 Gram Panchayat Shahpur, Pure Boodhi Upadhyay, District Sultanpur (Now Amethi)."
At the very outset learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn attention of this Court towards Annexure no. 8 which is an order dated 18.8.2022 passed by this Court in Writ-C No. 5395 of 2022 (Samar Jeet Singh vs. State of U.P. and others) in a writ petition filed before the Division Bench of this Court.

sentences.text:
For the convenience the order dated 18.8.2022 is being reproduced herein under :
"Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Standing Counsel for the State and Sri Prashant Arora learned counsel who has put in appearance on behalf of the opposite party no. 4.
It is an admitted position that gata no. 523 measuring 0.126(10 biswa) was handed over to the Basic Education Board for the purposes of construction of a junior high school in the area.
The transfer of land proceeded on the basis of an understanding that the petitioner shall be provided equal area of land in exchange.

In this regard,
necessary process was undertaken and a proposal for allotment of the land in exchange was also passed by the Land Management Committee which is yet to be acted upon.

Once the land in question was handed over to the Basic Education Board on the basis of a clear standing that the petitioner shall be provided equal area of land in exchange, there is no reason as to why the mutual understanding between the petitioner and the Basic Education Board may not be implemented by the district authorities.
Sri Prashant Arora learned counsel for the opposite party no. 4 has further informed that the matter is under active consideration of the district authorities.

sentences.text: Learned Standing Counsel has pointed out that the district authorities shall expedite the matter and necessary action shall be taken without any further delay.

We expect the authorities concerned to finalize the process of exchange expeditiously and preferably within a period of three months from the date of production of a certified copy of the order before the District Magistrate concerned.
In case of non-availability of land, it shall also be open to the District Magistrate to quantify and pay the compensation payable to the petitioner in lieu of the land already taken over.
The writ petition in terms of what has been observed herein-above is disposed of."

After the aforesaid order being passed when the competent revenue authority has not complied with the direction being issued by this Court, the petitioner filed a contempt petition bearing C.A.P.L. No.
77 of 2023 as the recital to this effect has been in given in para 20 of the writ petition.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has stated that when the notice has been issued in a contempt proceedings, the impugned order dated 28.12.2022 has been passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer,
Gauriganj, District Amethi by registering one case bearing Case No. 5160 of 2022 u/s 101 of U.P.
Revenue Code, 2006.

Learned counsel for the petitioner has stated that the petitioner had got no information regarding the aforesaid case inasmuch as the aforesaid case has probably been registered when the notices were issued by this Court in contempt proceedings.

In para 25,26 and 27 of the writ petition the petitioner has categorically indicated that the information of the aforesaid case has not been provided to the petitioner nor the petitioner was permitted to participate in a proceedings strictly in accordance with law.

He has further submitted that the compliance of Rule 101 and 102 of U.P. Land Revenue Rules, 2016 has not been followed and by means of ex-parte proceedings in the name of the petitioner the issue has been concluded making compliance of the order of this Court dated 18.8.2022, therefore, the impugned order is illegal and unwarranted and the same is violative of section 101 of the U.P. Revenue Code, 2006 and Rule 101 of the Rules, 2016.

Learned Addl. C.S.C. as well as learned counsel for the B.S.A. has, however, tried to justify the order by submitting that the aforesaid order has been passed in compliance of order dated 18.8.2022 passed by this Court but they could not justify the aforesaid order on the point that the aforesaid order has been passed without associating the petitioner in the proceedings and without affording an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner, rather a case in question has been registered in the name of the petitioner without informing him.

Be that as it may, since the Sub-Divisional Officer, Gauriganj, District Amethi has passed the impugned order dated 28.12.2022 in compliance of the order dated 18.8.2022 passed by this Court but the order dated 18.8.2022 of this Court does not entitled / authorize the competent revenue authority to register a case in the name of the petitioner without even informing him about the said case.

Further, while registering the case in the name of the petitioner at least the petitioner should have been given information to the effect that one case u/s 101 of Code, 2006 has been registered which is a mandatory condition of Rule 101 of the Rules, 2016.

sentences.text: it has nowhere been indicated that the petitioner or his counsel has been heard rather the aforesaid order only give recital of the facts and the final order has been passed.
Even no recital about the hearing of the learned counsel for the State has been given in the aforesaid order.
Therefore, the aforesaid impugned order dated 28.12.2022 suffers from illegality.

Further, there is error apparent on the face of the impugned order dated 28.12.2022 wherein the proceedings have been concluded in the name of the petitioner without informing the petitioner about the pendency of the case.
Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed.
The impugned order dated 28.12.2022 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer, Gauriganj, District Amethi in Case No. 5160 of 2022 ( Annexure no. 1 to the writ petition) is hereby set aside.

The matter is remanded back to the same authority to decide the case afresh strictly in accordance with law by affording an opportunity of hearing to the parties concerned with expedition preferably within a period of three months.
It is also directed that the parties shall cooperate in the proceedings and shall not take unnecessary adjournments.
No order as to costs.

.
